etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English princesse, a borrowing from Anglo-Norman princesse, Old French princesse. By surface analysis, prince +‎ -ess.

definitions.definition: A female member of a royal family other than a queen, especially a daughter or granddaughter of a monarch. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1872, George MacDonald, The Princess and the Goblin:
quote.text: She did not cry long, however, for she was as brave as could be expected of a princess of her age.

definitions.definition: A woman or girl who excels in a given field or class. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 2014, Blake Masters, Peter Thiel, Zero to One: Notes on Start Ups, or How to Build the Future:
quote.text: Michael Jackson was the king of pop. Britney Spears was the pop princess. Until they weren't.

definitions.definition: (now archaic) A female ruler or monarch; a queen. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 1596, Edmund Spenser, “Book V, Canto XII”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: And running all with greedie ioyfulnesse / To faire Irena, at her feet did fall, / And her adored with due humblenesse, / As their true Liege and Princesse naturall  […]

definitions.definition: The wife of a prince; the female ruler of a principality. [from 15th c.]
A young girl; used as a term of endearment. [from 18th c.]
(derogatory, chiefly US) A young girl or woman (or less commonly a man) who is vain, spoiled, or selfish; a prima donna. [from 20th c.]

quote.citation: 2020 September 15, Justmaiko, 2:13 from the start, in Trying Viral TikTok Life Hacks. **They Actually Work!!**‎[1]:
quote.text: Jonathan, if you hear this, you're a beautiful princess, but you're also a big, fat dork.

definitions.definition: A tinted crystal marble used in children's games.
A type of court card in the Tarot pack, coming between the 10 and the prince (Jack).
A Bulgarian open-faced baked sandwich prepared with ground meat.
